general_weights.name: Primary Products
general_weights.definition: Named product categories and concrete examples; multi-select.
general_weights.examples: Payroll software; industrial pumps; hamburgers

general_weights.name: Primary Services
general_weights.definition: Services sold to customers; distinguish services from internal support functions.
general_weights.examples: Payroll processing; equipment maintenance; freight forwarding

general_weights.name: Core Business Activity
general_weights.definition: Precise operating verb + output; distinguish ownership, manufacturing, distribution and licensing.
general_weights.examples: Manufactures pumps; licenses software; operates restaurants

general_weights.name: Customer Type
general_weights.definition: B2B / B2C / B2G / mixed; identify the paying customer separately from the end user.
general_weights.examples: B2B employers; B2C diners; B2G agencies

general_weights.name: Customer Segment
general_weights.definition: Specific buyer/user populations and roles; do not substitute an industry or a customer-size claim.
general_weights.examples: HR administrators; franchise operators; hospital procurement teams

general_weights.name: End Markets
general_weights.definition: Customer verticals or product applications; not the supplier’s own industry classification.
general_weights.examples: Healthcare providers; automotive production; consumer dining

general_weights.name: Customer Size
general_weights.definition: SMB / mid-market / enterprise / government / consumer / mixed; retain issuer definitions.
general_weights.examples: SMB employers; large enterprises; individual consumers

general_weights.name: Business Model
general_weights.definition: How operations are organized and value is delivered; distinguish from billing.
general_weights.examples: Franchisor; vertically integrated manufacturer; marketplace operator

general_weights.name: Revenue Model
general_weights.definition: What customers pay for and how revenue is earned; preserve multiple streams.
general_weights.examples: Subscription fees; product sales; transaction commissions

general_weights.name: Value Chain Position
general_weights.definition: Position in the supply/value chain and role relative to customers and suppliers.
general_weights.examples: Component supplier; OEM; wholesale distributor

general_weights.name: Geography Served
general_weights.definition: Markets actually served; distinguish customers/operations from headquarters.
general_weights.examples: U.S. customers; Europe and Asia; domestic-only operations

general_weights.name: Product Specialization
general_weights.definition: Breadth and focus of offerings, distinct from a product list or an unverified superiority claim.
general_weights.examples: Single therapeutic area; broad HCM suite; application-specific components

general_weights.name: Distribution Channels
general_weights.definition: How customers are reached and sales/orders acquired.
general_weights.examples: Direct sales; independent distributors; e-commerce

general_weights.name: Delivery Model
general_weights.definition: How the product/service is provided or deployed; distinguish from acquisition channel.
general_weights.examples: Cloud SaaS; on-premise installation; on-site managed service

general_weights.name: Pricing Structure
general_weights.definition: Charging unit and contractual pricing mechanism; avoid securities/debt pricing.
general_weights.examples: Per employee/month; fixed project fee; cost-plus contract

general_weights.name: Recurring Revenue Profile
general_weights.definition: Nature of repeat revenue; distinguish contracted recurrence from habitual repeat purchases.
general_weights.examples: Renewable subscriptions; usage-based recurring fees; repeat noncontractual purchases

general_weights.name: Customer Concentration
general_weights.definition: Named large-customer dependence or disclosed concentration; include period and denominator for figures.
general_weights.examples: Largest customer: 15% of annual revenue; diversified customer base

general_weights.name: Contract Duration
general_weights.definition: Customer/service/franchise contract term and renewal structure; exclude financing maturities.
general_weights.examples: Annual auto-renewal; three-year service term; month-to-month

general_weights.name: Capital Intensity
general_weights.definition: Owned/leased productive assets and investment needs; distinguish issuer assets from franchisee/supplier assets.
general_weights.examples: Owned factories; leased retail sites; outsourced production

general_weights.name: Regulatory Exposure
general_weights.definition: Applicable operating licenses, approvals and regulatory regimes; identify jurisdiction.
general_weights.examples: FDA device clearance; banking supervision; food-safety regulation

general_weights.name: Customer Switching Costs
general_weights.definition: Cited operational, contractual or integration barriers; do not assume high costs from tenure alone.
general_weights.examples: Data migration; workflow retraining; contractual termination fees

general_weights.name: Company Size Category
general_weights.definition: Supplier operating scale with dated evidence and units; not customer size or an unsupported size label.
general_weights.examples: 2,000 employees; 300 operated stores; annual revenue in stated currency

general_weights.name: Labor Intensity
general_weights.definition: Dependence on labor, specialist personnel or billable capacity.
general_weights.examples: Clinician-led care; technician-intensive service; automated production

general_weights.name: Revenue Cyclicality
general_weights.definition: Documented demand sensitivity, seasonality or cycle exposure; distinguish observed history from inference.
general_weights.examples: Construction-cycle demand; holiday seasonality; commodity-linked demand

general_weights.name: Supply Chain Complexity
general_weights.definition: Sourcing dependencies, concentration, lead times and procurement structure.
general_weights.examples: Single-source component; global supplier network; cooperative purchasing

general_weights.name: Technology Dependence
general_weights.definition: Operational reliance on technology/platforms; being in technology is not proof of a specific dependency.
general_weights.examples: Third-party cloud infrastructure; proprietary transaction platform

general_weights.name: Geographic Concentration
general_weights.definition: Dependence on particular markets; distinguish from the list of countries served.
general_weights.examples: 80% of annual revenue in the U.S.; concentrated in one state

general_weights.name: Product Differentiation
general_weights.definition: Specific product/service differences with evidence; label issuer marketing claims.
general_weights.examples: Patented process; industry-specific workflow; custom-engineered design

general_weights.name: IP Dependence
general_weights.definition: Material dependence on patents, licenses, proprietary technology or other protected rights.
general_weights.examples: Licensed drug rights; patent-protected process; proprietary software

general_weights.name: Brand Dependence
general_weights.definition: Role of brand, trademark, licensing and customer recognition; distinguish documented model from assumed brand strength.
general_weights.examples: Licensed consumer brand; branded franchise system; private-label supplier

general_weights.name: Competitive Positioning
general_weights.definition: Attributable positioning/share claims with date, geography and market definition; label self-descriptions.
general_weights.examples: Issuer-described niche leader; independently measured category share

general_weights.name: Company Maturity
general_weights.definition: Operating stage and relevant business history; incorporation date alone does not establish maturity.
general_weights.examples: Commercial-stage business; pre-revenue development; established operating platform

facet_anchors.100: Same economically relevant role, offering and customer need with source support
facet_anchors.75: Close substitute with a material but limited difference
facet_anchors.50: Adjacent business with both meaningful overlap and material differences
facet_anchors.25: Weak overlap, mainly broad industry or terminology

target_rule: Only allowed official business website evidence and instructor Revenue/EBITDA/Debt; no hidden vendor/SEC/segment inputs
